summary: The Android screen-share setup now explains that an app-only projection can hide its image when the selected app is fully covered or the user switches away. This distinguishes expected Android privacy behavior from a broken full-display stream. Setup guidance is hidden when only changing quality; the old redundant system-permission prompt copy remains absent.

checks.name: Android setup privacy guidance regression
checks.observation: All 12 screen-share quality/picker tests pass, including new capture guidance and hidden guidance while changing quality.

checks.name: Flutter analyzer
checks.observation: No diagnostics in changed files. Two existing info diagnostics remain in vendored flutter_webrtc: unnecessary library name and runtime type check on a JS interop DOMException.

checks.name: Pixel UI and capture-mode acceptance
checks.observation: No active MediaProjection was present in the latest read-only snapshot. No screen content was captured and the user-owned projection was not started or stopped by the agent.

checks.name: Spec traceability
checks.observation: The host has neither pwsh nor powershell; the script could not be executed.

limitations: This is guidance only; it does not alter Android MediaProjection privacy behavior or prove that a black frame during full-display capture is fixed.

Android documents that the selected region becomes invisible when its app is fully covered or the user navigates away: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/projection/MediaProjection.Callback#onCapturedContentVisibilityChanged(boolean).
remaining: Verify the copy and layout on Pixel 7. Compare app-only capture while the selected app is visible/hidden against full-display capture, and record room membership plus sender/receiver video counters. FE-59 and FE-64 remain open.
